pairs: Moyses autem pascebat oves Jethro soceri sui sacerdotis Madian:
Now Moses was pasturing the sheep of his father-in-law Jethro, a priest of Midian.
cumque minasset gregem ad interiora deserti,
And when he had driven the flock into the interior of the desert,
he came to the mountain of God, Horeb.
Apparuitque ei Dominus in flamma ignis de medio rubi:
And the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush.
And he saw that the bush was burning
“I will go and see this great sight,
why the bush is not burnt.”
Cernens autem Dominus quod pergeret ad videndum,
Then the Lord, discerning that he proceeded on to see it,
called to him from the midst of the bush,
remove the shoes from your feet.
locus enim, in quo stas, terra sancta est.
For the place on which you stand is holy ground.”
“I am the God of your father:
non enim audebat aspicere contra Deum.
for he dared not look directly at God.
And the Lord said to him:
Vidi afflictionem populi mei in Ægypto,
“I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt,
et clamorem ejus audivi propter duritiam eorum qui præsunt operibus:
and I have heard their outcry because of the harshness of those who are over the works.
descendi ut liberem eum de manibus Ægyptiorum,
I have descended in order to free them from the hands of the Egyptians,
et educam de terra illa in terram bonam,
and to lead them from that land into a good and spacious land,
into a land which flows with milk and honey,
in terram quæ fluit lacte et melle,
to the places of the Canaanite,
Clamor ergo filiorum Israël venit ad me:
And so, the outcry of the sons of Israel has come to me.
And I have seen their affliction,
with which they are oppressed by the Egyptians.
and I will send you to Pharaoh,
so that you may lead my people,
Quis sum ego ut vadam ad Pharaonem,
“Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh
et educam filios Israël de Ægypto?
and that I should lead the sons of Israel out of Egypt?”
et hoc habebis signum, quod miserim te:
And you will have this as a sign that I have sent you:
cum eduxeris populum meum de Ægypto,
When you will have brought my people out of Egypt,
you will offer sacrifice to God upon this mountain.”
Ecce ego vadam ad filios Israël, et dicam eis:
I will go to the sons of Israel, and I will say to them,
Deus patrum vestrorum misit me ad vos.
‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you.’
Quod est nomen ejus? quid dicam eis?
‘What is his name?’ What shall I say to them?”
“Thus shall you say to the sons of Israel:
Qui est, misit me ad vos.
‘HE WHO IS has sent me to you.’”
Dixitque iterum Deus ad Moysen: Hæc dices filiis Israël:
And God said again to Moses: “Thus shall you say to the sons of Israel:
the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob,
hoc nomen mihi est in æternum,
This is the name for me in eternity,
et hoc memoriale meum in generationem et generationem.
and this is my memorial from generation to generation.
Go and gather together the elders of Israel,
and you shall say to them:
Dominus Deus patrum vestrorum apparuit mihi,
‘The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham,
and the God of Jacob, has appeared to me,
When visiting, I have visited you,
et vidi omnia quæ acciderunt vobis in Ægypto.
and I have seen all that has befallen you in Egypt.
Et dixi ut educam vos de afflictione Ægypti in terram Chananæi,
And I have spoken in order to lead you out of the affliction of Egypt,
into the land of the Canaanite,
into a land flowing with milk and honey.’
And they shall hear your voice.
you and the elders of Israel,
and you shall say to him:
‘The Lord God of the Hebrews has called us.
ibimus viam trium dierum in solitudinem,
We shall go three days’ journey into the wilderness,
in order to offer sacrifice to the Lord our God.’
Sed ego scio quod non dimittet vos rex Ægypti ut eatis nisi per manum validam.
But I know that the king of Egypt will not release you, unless you go out by a powerful hand.
For I will extend my hand,
et percutiam Ægyptum in cunctis mirabilibus meis,
and I will strike Egypt with all my wonders that I will do in the midst of them.
quæ facturus sum in medio eorum:
Daboque gratiam populo huic coram Ægyptiis:
And I will grant favor to this people in the sight of the Egyptians.
And so, when you go forth,
you shall not go out empty.
sed postulabit mulier a vicina sua et ab hospita sua, vasa argentea et aurea,
But every woman shall ask of her neighbor and of her hostess vessels of silver and of gold,
ac vestes: ponetisque eas super filios et filias vestras,
